stops.note: from the root of German 'Liebe', Latin 'libido' and the old English word 'lief', dear
used for both human affection and the love of God in Old English sermons and poems
'love' meaning zero in games is recorded from the 1740s, perhaps from playing 'for love', not money; the tale that it is French 'l'œuf', egg, is doubtful
